description: Split workflow-activity graph editor orchestration into focused session, save-flow, and controller hooks plus a thin React Flow card viewport—preserving all operator-visible edit, save, leave, and validation behavior while aligning domain logic with factory-graph-editor and session save with useFactoryDocumentSave.

context.customerAsk: Split graph editor hooks and card layers. Soft program dependency: factory-validation-consolidation (V) for draft validation API. Full spec: tasks/prd-ui-graph-editor-orchestration-split.md
context.problem: The current-activity graph editor composes editor mode, tools, add/connect/remove controllers, save and leave confirmation, classifier gating, draft validation, and editable factory graph state across large hook and card files with duplicated test mocks—making changes risky and blurring domain, session UX, and viewport responsibilities.
context.solution: Reorganize into factory-graph-editor (draft, operations, projection, save input), workflow-activity graph-editor hooks (session mode/tools, save/leave, controllers), and thin card components (React Flow wiring only). Prove zero operator-visible regression with existing hook/card tests, a shared graph-editor test harness, browser verification on the full edit path, and an optional validationTargets extension point for program V without default UI change.

acceptanceCriteria: Operators retain identical graph edit mode, tools, connect/remove/add, save, discard, and leave/confirm behavior including active-work save block and classifier unsupported gating
Save persists canonical factory document with version via shared useFactoryDocumentSave / REPLACE_CURRENT path
Draft validation in edit mode still debounces, aborts stale requests, and refreshes markers after graph mutations without incorrect interaction blocking
factory-graph-editor owns domain; workflow-activity hooks own session UX; card TSX stays composition-only with no new inline domain mutations
Graph editor tests pass without weakened assertions; shared graph-editor-harness reduces duplicated mock setup in largest editor tests
Typecheck, lint, and UI tests pass (quality gate)

userStories.title: Editor session mode and interaction gating
userStories.description: As an operator editing the factory graph, I need edit mode and tools to enable only when the factory document is ready and editable in-graph so I am not misled into mutating an unsupported or loading graph.
acceptanceCriteria: Entering edit mode enables graph interaction when the current factory document query succeeded and no classifier workstation blocks in-graph editing; leaving edit mode clears the active tool
While the factory document is loading or save is pending, graph edit interactions stay disabled even if edit mode is on
When a classifier workstation blocks the graph editor, entering edit mode has no effect and unavailable treatment matches pre-split behavior
Active tool selection drives connection/removal/add flows the same as before (one tool mode at a time)
Session orchestration is implemented in useGraphEditorSession; useCurrentActivityGraphEditor composes it without changing the public return shape used by the card
Existing hook tests for mode toggle and interaction gating pass without assertion weakening
Typecheck passes
Tests pass

userStories.title: Save, discard, and leave confirmation flows
userStories.description: As an operator with pending graph edits, I need save, discard, and leave flows to behave exactly as today—including confirmations and blocked save when work is active.
acceptanceCriteria: Saving from the editor persists via the shared factory document save hook; success closes confirm-save UI; failure leaves the operator in edit mode with the same error treatment as today
Save stays blocked with the same user-visible reason when factory work is in flight or the draft is stale
Leaving edit mode with unsaved changes opens leave confirmation; discard reverts the draft and exits; save-and-leave saves then exits
Discard pending changes clears transient editor state (connection notice, pending removal, confirm dialogs) without unintended mode exit
Save/leave orchestration lives in useGraphEditorSaveFlow using existing save-summary and active-work guards from factory-graph-editor lib
Document-plane and save/leave hook tests pass without assertion weakening
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
